learning_outcomes.text: Students understand the relationship between material structure and properties of metallic materials by acquiring knowledge about the material structure and its changes due to alloying elements.
Students understand the deformation behavior, transformation behavior, and phase reactions.
Students develop skills to apply and evaluate material characteristic values for different operating conditions and transfer them to component design.

Students develop the competence to measure and evaluate material properties within the framework of a materials test and to specifically induce changes in material behavior through heat treatments or mechanical deformation.
Students use the acquired knowledge to select suitable materials for various applications.

syllabus_topics: Lattice defects and their effect on material behavior
Deformation and fracture: strength, toughness, ductility
Alloying: phase diagrams and iron-carbon diagram
Properties and material behavior of selected steel materials such as structural steels, tool steels, cast iron
Fundamental experiments on metallic materials will be deepened illustratively in practical courses
assessment_rules: Credit points are awarded upon successful completion of the module examination.
